summary: Generates audio-style ADSR envelopes from input trigger threshold crossings or explicit trigger pulses.
key_concepts: Trigger CHOP starts audio-style ADSR envelopes from input threshold crossings or explicit Trigger pulses.
The envelope stages are delay, attack, peak, decay, sustain, and release.
Trigger and release thresholds can be shared or separated, and Trigger On chooses increasing or decreasing crossings.
Peak and sustain levels are independent, but peak can never be lower than sustain.
Complete Envelope controls whether release can terminate the envelope early, while Remainder controls unfinished samples.
For a full static waveform, Time Slice must be off and no input should be connected.

key_params.name: threshold
key_params.note: Use trigger threshold as release threshold

key_params.name: retrigger
key_params.note: Delay before a new trigger may occur

key_params.name: triggeron
key_params.note: Trigger on increasing or decreasing values

key_params.name: multitrigger
key_params.note: Ignore, add, or restart on multiple triggers

key_params.name: clamppeak
key_params.note: Clamp additive multi-trigger values to peak

key_params.name: remainder
key_params.note: Discard, extend, or mix unfinished envelope remainder

common_gotchas: Triggers occur when the first input crosses the trigger threshold, commonly 0 to 1.
Peak value can never be less than sustain value.
For a full static waveform, turn off Time Slice and leave the input disconnected.
Works with both time-sliced inputs and static channels.
For jittery inputs, use a Count CHOP style delay/threshold guard before Trigger CHOP.
Timer CHOP or Event CHOP may be a better planner target for general process timing.
